title: Silas and the Bridge
premise: In 1893, on a storm-battered coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Kestrel Villalobos keeps the town's records in her late husband's workshop, believing history belongs to capitals and battlefields, not to her gray promontory. When the army requisitions the town for coastal defense and seizes the ledger holding every family's name, deeds, and debts, Kestrel discovers the requisition is a land grab disguised as war preparedness — and that her own name has been quietly erased from the record. Over one brutal winter she rebuilds the ledger from memory, testimony, and salvaged pages, racing against demolition orders while the young officer assigned to inventory the town begins to doubt his orders. The workshop burns in the final storm; Kestrel saves the reconstructed ledger, exposes the corruption at a military tribunal, and wins back the town's names — though not the workshop — learning that history happens wherever someone refuses to be written out of it.
about_author: Kestrel Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal municipal records before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about ordinary people whose names survive only because someone bothered to write them down.

chapters.title: The Light and the Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Establishes her solitary routine tending the light and maintaining her husband Tomás's ledger of the town's names, births, debts, and deeds in his workshop below the cliff. She dismisses rumors of war preparations as news for other people. Emotional beat: quiet grief and comfortable detachment, about to be shattered.

chapters.title: Ships at the Horizon
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Warships anchor off the point; an army column marches into town under Major Halloway, who announces the requisition and posts seizure notices. The townsfolk assume it's temporary. Kestrel notices soldiers measuring the harbor, not the coastline. Emotional beat: unease hardening into suspicion as the familiar world is fenced off.

chapters.title: What the Paper Says
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The requisition order claims the town was never properly incorporated — no legal record of its names exists. Soldiers confiscate the ledger from the workshop. Kestrel realizes the 'missing' incorporation papers were destroyed years ago by a land speculator now advising Halloway. Emotional beat: cold fury; history as a weapon.

chapters.title: Lieutenant Ashe
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Elias Ashe's POV. The young officer assigned to inventory the town finds discrepancies: the seizure maps predate the war order by months. He interviews Kestrel, who tests him with pointed questions he can't answer honestly. Emotional beat: Ashe's first crack of doubt; two wary adversaries circling each other.

chapters.title: Names from Memory
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel begins reconstructing the ledger from memory, going door to door collecting testimonies while soldiers watch. Old Marta recalls deeds no one else remembers; the fisherfolk contribute dates and debts. Emotional beat: reluctant community becoming conspirators; belonging forged through shared resistance.

chapters.title: The Speculator's Shadow
chapters.summary: Ashe's POV. Ashe traces the speculator Corven's paper trail to a syndicate buying requisitioned land cheap. Halloway warns him off; his reports begin disappearing. He secretly copies documents, torn between career and conscience. Emotional beat: corruption revealed from inside; power shown corrupting everyone it touches.

chapters.title: What the Storm Took
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A soldier raids the workshop searching for the reconstruction; Kestrel hides the half-finished ledger inside the lighthouse's oil store. Tomás's letters surface, revealing he suspected the land scheme before his death. Emotional beat: grief rekindled and repurposed — her husband's work becomes her mission.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel and Ashe POVs. The great storm arrives with the demolition order. The workshop burns under suspicious circumstances; Ashe defies orders to help Kestrel salvage the completed ledger and Corven's documents from the flames. Emotional beat: climax of loss and loyalty; the fire destroys the past but not the proof.

chapters.title: Tribunal
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the military tribunal, Kestrel presents the reconstructed ledger and names every family aloud while Corven's forged papers are read into the record. Halloway disavows Corven; the requisition collapses. Emotional beat: triumph without gloating — the power of the spoken name against institutional erasure.

chapters.title: Keeper of Names
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Spring comes; the army withdraws, the town incorporates properly at last, and the new ledger is signed by every household. Kestrel remains keeper of the light and of the book, teaching a young apprentice her husband's methods. Emotional beat: resolution and belonging — history made hers, kept by hand, one name at a time.
